Needs changes before merge.

Safety-tier review. I built and tested locally on macOS. I trial-merged the head with upstream main `cced2e6fde64825399ac1c9eb42c8aed15f27b9a`. The merge was clean. I used that main revision's AGENTS.md for the law check.

The generator now carries the Back bore dwell and uses the plunge feed in both directions. The two new tests detect both old behaviours. No golden, fixture, importer, UI, dependency or process file changed. No golden required a line-by-line check. No screenshots are required.

Command: `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test dwell_cycles_modal_p --test haas_dwell_cycles --test mach4_post --test heidenhain_cycles`.

The test-data and importer rules require no further suites for this diff.

**Mutations rerun**

1. I restored `p.feed` on the Back bore retract. `back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed` failed at `tests_backbore.rs:70`:

   ```text
   left: Some(500.0)
   right: Some(100.0)
   ```

2. I removed `CycleKind::BackBore` from the dwell list. `back_bore_carries_the_dwell` failed at `tests_backbore.rs:48`:

   ```text
   G89 dwells at the bottom: the cycle record carries the user's 1.5 s, got 0
   ```

I restored the source. Both tests then passed. The review worktree had no source diff after restoration.

**Requested before merge**

1. `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs:193`: Add the missing Sinumerik G89 dwell pin. This change lets a generated Back bore send a positive dwell to that post. The listed post tests do not cover its G89 P word. Issue #1480 requires a pinned P unit for each canned post. The PR body records this missing check, but proposes a follow-up. Add the test in `crates/post/tests/`. Pin the nonzero P word and the transition to zero dwell. Record the unit source, or refuse the dwell by name if the post cannot support it. The [Siemens ISO dialects Function Manual](https://cache.industry.siemens.com/dl/files/254/109801254/att_1077768/v1/ONE_840Dsl_828D_iso_dialects_fct_man_0721_en-US.pdf), table 6-1 on printed page 95, includes the G89 dwell unit. This is a missing regression check; this review does not prove that the current unit is wrong.

2. `AGENTS.md:601` on upstream main; PR body, “Not exercised”: Update the body with the heavy-lane results for the final head. It still says that no heavy lane ran. The law requires the body to name the reached lanes that ran. Record motion heavy and app heavy, the tested head, and the results before the PR is marked ready. The local run above gives review evidence for this head trial-merged with main.

No approval, merge or push was made. A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

1. Added the Sinumerik G89 dwell unit and zero-transition pins. The post now writes P0 to clear a previous dwell. The source is the Siemens ISO dialects Function Manual, table 6-1, page 95, and section 6.3.1. Tests: `sinumerik_g89_dwell_posts_p_in_milliseconds` and `sinumerik_g89_zero_dwell_clears_previous_p`. Each mutation failed as expected. Each restored test passed.
2. Updated the PR body with the heavy results for the final head. Both reached lanes ran: motion heavy and app heavy. The gate passed 217 steps with 0 failed steps. Motion passed 56 tests. App passed 42 tests. The gate accepted three expected failures for #1950.

Head: `766540356cab0fc156ea47466977f9432e0eeae4`.

Quick gate: PASS, 69 steps, 0 failed. Clippy: PASS for motion and post, all targets, with warnings denied.

Please re-review this head.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 766540356cab0fc156ea47466977f9432e0eeae4 -->
Read-only second review (Opus). Not built here.

Verdict: Ready to merge.

I read the full diff of head `766540356` against `origin/main`. I also read the onCycle code of each post that handles `BACKBORE`, and the earlier review thread.

**Blockers**

None.

**What I checked**

- `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs:170-177`: the Back bore chain now feeds in and feeds out at `p.plunge_feed`. This agrees with the single F word of G89 and of the G85 that the Fanuc family, grblHAL, LinuxCNC and Tormach write for zero dwell. The chain stays a `Feed` move up, not a rapid. The Ream chain uses the same law.
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs:188-196`: `BackBore` is added to the dwell list. Each post that handles `BACKBORE` writes the dwell in its own unit, writes it as an explicit dwell block (Heidenhain, Carvera, TinyG), or refuses the Back bore by name (lathe posts). I found no post that drops the dwell silently.
- `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:797`: G89 now always writes `P<ms>`, also `P0`. The ms value is `Math.round(p.P * 1000)`, the same scale as G82 and G83. The G73, G84, G85 and G86 refusals run before this line, so the new `|| g === "G89"` term cannot add a P to a refused cycle. The modal reset is correct: each G89 block carries its own P.
- The earlier finding 1 of the first review is met. `crates/post/tests/sinumerik_g89_dwell.rs` pins `P500` and the transition to `P0`, and names the Siemens source.
- The earlier finding 2 is met. The PR body names the reached heavy lanes (motion heavy, app heavy), their results and the tested head.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. The new uses are in test files only.
- No test became weaker. The old Back bore assertion in `drilling/tests.rs` ("back-bore retracts on a feed") stays and still holds.
- File sizes: `cycle.rs` is 259 lines. The new files are 77 and 107 lines.
- Test placement: the generator pins are in `camcraft-motion`. The post pins are in `crates/post/tests/` and import only `camcraft_post`. The new post test has a provenance line and a Gate map line.
- `docs/decisions/1480-backbore-dwell.md` has the `## #N - <title>` format and the four parts.
- The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends with `Fixes #1480`.

**Non-blocking notes**

1. `assets/posts/mach4.cps:786` and `:814`: Mach4 writes G89 for each Back bore and writes P only when the dwell is positive. Before this PR, a generated Back bore always had zero dwell. Now a program can post `G89 ... P0.25`, then `G80`, then a later `G89` with no P. If Mach4 keeps P modal after G80, the second hole dwells too. The first review asked for this check on Sinumerik only. I recommend a follow-up issue: write `P0` on each Mach4 G89, or post G85 at zero dwell as the Fanuc family does. Pin the transition as `sinumerik_g89_zero_dwell_clears_previous_p` does. The extra dwell is not a gouge, so I do not hold this PR for it.
2. `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:797`: the same modal concern applies to G83 on Sinumerik. A G83 with a dwell, then a G83 with no dwell, writes no P on the second block. This is older than this PR (#2349). A follow-up issue can pin it.
3. Issue #1480 asks that programs with no dwell post byte-identical. Two outputs change on purpose: the Sinumerik G89 block gets `P0`, and the `.cl` chain and the Heidenhain explicit chain feed out at the plunge feed. The PR body and the decision file record both changes. No golden moved.
4. Issue #1480 has the `enhancement` label, and the PR type is `fix`. The CL chain disagreed with the posted F word, so `fix` is a fair type. The merging session can keep it.
